newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki turns to lower close on early U.S. dip.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki turns to lower close on early U.S. dip.

text.p: Finnish shares traded a shade up almost the whole session on Tuesday in thin trade due to a U.S. holiday on Monday, but turned lower just before closing as Wall Street dipped in early dealings, brokers said.
Wall Street stocks fell on higher interest rates, and Helsinki's attention turned there, after closely tracking EMU nerves as the week started after the French elections.
The FOX index fell 0.43 to 1,070.70 points and the HEX lost 0.37 percent to 3,094.02, but bourse engine Nokia closed up 0.40 markka at 351.40.

Engineering group Metra was active and traded higher most session though it closed flat, and brokers said it has been lagging the market and was now starting to catch up. "It seems the trend could start to go higher," one broker said.
Finnlines hit a new life-high at 144.80 markka -- up 4.30 markka -- but closed up 2.00 markka at 142.50 markka.

The stock has been rising steadily since Finnlines reported Jan-Apr earnings last week. Compared to May 20, the day before it announced first tertial earnings near the highest forecast, it has risen six percent.

Cultor, which reports Jan-Apr on Wednesday, and Konecranes, which comes on Thursday, both fell: some analysts have lowered earnings estimates for the period after both companies warned their estimates looked too high.
Cultor's more liquid X series ended off 1.50 markka at 283.50, Konecranes was down 3.00 at 195.00.
